title: How can you practise case interviews on your own?
description: A practical routine for building case interview skills alone: what you can practise solo, a 30-minute daily plan and how to do a full case by yourself.
hook: Not everyone has a friend who can give them cases, and that is fine. A lot of case skill can be built on your own, in short sessions. Here is a routine that works.
body:
What you can build on your own

  • Structuring: two-minute drills against a model answer
  • Maths: short daily sums, out loud
  • Charts: one chart a day, insight in one sentence
  • Fit: writing and rehearsing your stories
  • Voice: short warm-ups and recording yourself

A 30-minute daily routine

  1. 5 minutes: a voice or thinking warm-up.
  2. 10 minutes: three structuring prompts from a practice set.
  3. 10 minutes: mental maths or one sizing question.
  4. 5 minutes: say one recommendation out loud and record it.

Do a full case on your own

Pick a case, read the prompt, and talk through it as if someone were listening: recap, structure, ask for data (then read it), do the maths, and give a recommendation. It feels strange at first. It works. Afterwards, write down one thing to fix next time.

When to find a partner

Practising alone builds skill. Practising with someone builds comfort under pressure. Aim for at least a few cases with another person before the real thing, even a friend with no business background can read you a case.

A solo session with a measurable output

Set a 35-minute timer. Spend 3 minutes understanding a fictional case, 4 minutes drawing a structure, 15 minutes examining exhibits or making assumptions and calculations, 3 minutes recording a recommendation, and 10 minutes reviewing. You can use a public practice case or write a short original prompt yourself, such as a regional bus operator trying to reduce delays.

The essential ingredient is feedback. Before viewing any model answer, record what you said and identify one missed branch, one mathematical error, and one part where you did not explain the implication. Then replay the opening and conclusion. "My analysis was weak" is vague; "I never asked whether delays were concentrated on two routes" is specific enough to fix.

Solo practice is excellent for structuring, arithmetic, exhibit reading and communication. It is less reliable for practising how you respond to interruptions or surprise information. Add occasional sessions with another person once you can complete a full case alone. That way, solo work builds foundations and partner work tests them under realistic conditions.
outro: Every case in the free casebook has an interviewer script, so a friend can run it for you too. Next in this topic: How should you prepare if your case interview is one week away?
